You are rapid_thistle87, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. ## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll inspect the bundled docs and available CLI behavior first, then implement the highest coverage paths and coordinate findings with the group.

Make sure to read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first! # Introduction Taplo CLI aims to be an one stop shop tool for working with TOML files via the command line. The features include validation, formatting, and querying TOML documents with a [jq](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/)-like fashion. # Formatting It is possible to format files in-place or via standard i/o. ```sh taplo fmt foo.toml ``` Or ```sh cat foo.toml | taplo fmt - ``` ::: info By default Taplo will bail on documents that contain syntax errors to avoid destructive edits, you can use the `--force` flag to suppress this and try to format the invalid document(s) anyway. ::: ## Options Formatter options are read from the [configuration file](./configuration.md#configuration-file), on top of that it is possible to specify overrides via the `--option` flag: ```sh taplo fmt --option indent_tables=false foo.toml ``` ## Check It is possible to check whether the given files are properly formatted via the `--check` flag. When this flag is supplied, no formatting will be done. # Conversion and Extraction Taplo makes it easy to convert TOML files to JSON and also extract specific values via the `get` command. ## Examples The following examples use the TOML file below: ```toml # foo.toml [foo] bar = true [[baz]] baz_field = "baz 1" [[baz]] baz_field = "baz 2" ``` ## Converting to JSON ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml -o json ``` This will yield the following output: ```json { "foo": { "bar": true }, "baz": [ { "baz_field": "baz 1" }, { "baz_field": "baz 2" } ] } ``` ## Extracting Specific Values It is possible to extract specific values via a simple query expressions. ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml 'baz[1].baz_field' ``` This will yield: ``` baz 2 ``` ::: warning Expressions with array patterns `[]` might need to be put between quotation marks for some shells. ::: ::: info List indexing is 0-based. ::: By default the value will be "parsed", so that no strings will contain escape sequences or quotation marks. Taplo supports validation of TOML files, by default it will only look for syntax errors and some semantic errors such as duplicate keys.

```sh
taplo check foo.toml
```

## Schema Validation

Taplo supports validation via [JSON Schemas](https://json-schema.org) (Draft 4).

### Using a Specific Schema

```sh
taplo check --schema https://example.com/foo-schema.json foo.toml
```

### Using a Schema Catalog

Taplo supports schema catalogs such as the [JSON Schema Store](https://www.schemastore.org/json/) for retrieving schemas and matching them to files via file names.

You can enable this by either specifying a catalog via the `--schema-catalog` flag, or enabling the use of the default catalogs via `--default-schema-catalogs`.
# Configuration

## Log Level

Taplo uses the Rust `tracing` library for configurable logging features and respects the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. All logs regardless of log level are printed to the standard error output.

In most cases you might wish to disable logging below a certain log level.
As an example if you wish to only see error messages, you can do the following:

```sh
RUST_LOG=error taplo lint foo.toml
```

The available log levels:

- `trace`
- `debug`
- `info`
- `warn`
- `error`

+"""Small, dependency-free implementation of Taplo's common formatting behavior."""
+import re
+
+def format_text(src, options=None):
+    opts = {"compact_entries": False, "compact_arrays": True, "array_trailing_comma": True,
+            "trailing_newline": True, "crlf": False, "allowed_blank_lines": 2}
+    opts.update(options or {})
+    # Normalize line endings, then format each statement while retaining comments and table order.
+    lines = src.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").split("\n")
+    out=[]
+    blank=0
+    for line in lines:
+        s=line.strip()
+        if not s:
+            blank += 1
+            if blank <= int(opts.get("allowed_blank_lines", 2)) and out and out[-1] != "": out.append("")
+            continue
+        blank=0
+        if s.startswith("#") or (s.startswith("[") and s.endswith("]")):
+            out.append(s); continue
+        # Locate assignment = outside quoted strings and nested values.
+        quote=None; esc=False; depth=0; eq=-1
+        for i,c in enumerate(s):
+            if quote:
+                if esc: esc=False
+                elif c=='\\' and quote=='"': esc=True
+                elif c==quote: quote=None
+            elif c in ('"', "'"): quote=c
+            elif c in "[{(": depth+=1
+            elif c in "]})": depth-=1
+            elif c=="=" and depth==0: eq=i; break
+        if eq >= 0:
+            key=s[:eq].strip(); val=s[eq+1:].strip()
+            # Normalize whitespace around separators inside arrays/inline tables without changing strings.
+            val=_normalize(val, bool(opts.get("compact_arrays", True)), bool(opts.get("compact_entries", False)))
+            s=key + ("=" if opts.get("compact_entries") else " = ") + val
+        out.append(s)
+    while out and out[-1]=="": out.pop()
+    result="\n".join(out)
+    if opts.get("trailing_newline", True) and result: result += "\n"
+    if opts.get("crlf"): result=result.replace("\n","\r\n")
+    return result
+
+def _normalize(s, compact_arrays, compact_entries):
+    # Token-wise whitespace normalization for arrays and inline tables.
+    res=[]; quote=None; esc=False
+    for i,c in enumerate(s):
+        if quote:
+            res.append(c)
+            if esc: esc=False
+            elif c=='\\' and quote=='"': esc=True
+            elif c==quote: quote=None
+            continue
+        if c in ('"',"'"): quote=c; res.append(c); continue
+        if c=='[':
+            res.append("[" if compact_arrays else "[ ")
+            continue
+        if c==']':
+            if compact_arrays and res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
+            res.append("]"); continue
+        if c=='{': res.append("{" + ("" if compact_arrays else " ")); continue
+        if c=='}':
+            if res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
+            res.append("}"); continue
+        if c==',':
+            while res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
+            res.append(", "); continue
+        if c=='=':
+            while res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
+            res.append("=" if compact_entries else " = "); continue
+        if c=='#':
+            while res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
+            res.append(" #"); res.extend(s[i+1:]); break
+        if c.isspace():
+            if not res or res[-1] in "[{,= ": continue
+            res.append(" "); continue
+        if res and res[-1]==' ' and compact_arrays and c in "]}": res.pop()
+        res.append(c)
+    return ''.join(res).strip()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import sys
+
+def _format(args):
+    import format_impl
+    opts={}; files=[]; check=False; diff=False; force=False; i=0
+    while i<len(args):
+        a=args[i]
+        if a in ("-h","--help"):
+            sys.stdout.write("Format TOML documents.\n\nUsage: taplo format [OPTIONS] [FILES]...\n"); return 0
+        if a in ("--check",): check=True
+        elif a=="--diff": diff=True
+        elif a in ("-f","--force"): force=True
+        elif a in ("-o","--option"):
+            i+=1
+            if i>=len(args): return 2
+            pair=args[i]
+            if "=" not in pair: return 1
+            k,v=pair.split("=",1)
+            if v.lower() in ("true","false"): opts[k]=v.lower()=="true"
+            elif v.isdigit(): opts[k]=int(v)
+            else: opts[k]=v.strip("\"'")
+        elif a.startswith("--option="):
+            pair=a[len("--option="):]
+            if "=" not in pair:return 1
+            k,v=pair.split("=",1); opts[k]= v.lower()=="true" if v.lower() in ("true","false") else (int(v) if v.isdigit() else v.strip("\"'"))
+        elif a.startswith("-") and a!="-":
+            if a in ("-c","--config","--cache-path","--stdin-filepath","--colors"):
+                i+=1
+            elif a.startswith("--"): pass
+            else: return 2
+        else: files.append(a)
+        i+=1
+    if not files or files==["-"]:
+        src=sys.stdin.read()
+        out=format_impl.format_text(src,opts)
+        if check: return 1 if src!=out else 0
+        if diff:
+            import difflib
+            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(src.splitlines(True),out.splitlines(True),fromfile="",tofile=""))
+        else: sys.stdout.write(out)
+        return 0
+    import glob
+    paths=[]
+    for f in files: paths.extend(glob.glob(f) or [f])
+    rc=0
+    for path in paths:
+        try:
+            with open(path,encoding="utf-8",newline="") as h: src=h.read()
+            out=format_impl.format_text(src,opts)
+            if check:
+                if src!=out: rc=1
+            elif diff:
+                import difflib
+                sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(src.splitlines(True),out.splitlines(True),fromfile=path,tofile=path))
+            else:
+                with open(path,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="") as h: h.write(out)
+        except OSError as e:
+            print(str(e),file=sys.stderr); rc=1
+    return rc
+
+def main(argv):
+    if not argv or argv[0] in ("-h","--help","help"):
+        sys.stdout.write("Usage: taplo [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>\n\nCommands: lint, format, lsp, config, get, toml-test, completions\n"); return 0
+    if argv[0] in ("-V","--version"):
+        print("taplo 0.9.3"); return 0
+    cmd=argv.pop(0)
+    if cmd in ("format","fmt"): return _format(argv)
+    if cmd in ("config","cfg"):
+        import config_cmd
+        config_cmd.run(argv); return 0
+    if cmd=="completions":
+        import completions
+        return completions.run(argv[0] if argv else "")
+    if cmd=="toml-test":
+        import tomltest
+        for line in sys.stdin:
+            try: print(tomltest.decode(line))
+            except Exception: return 1
+        return 0
+    # Command modules are optional while the group is integrating implementations.
+    modname={"lint":"lint_impl","check":"lint_impl","validate":"lint_impl","get":"get_impl","lsp":"lsp_impl"}.get(cmd)
+    if modname:
+        try:
+            mod=__import__(modname)
+            result=mod.run(argv)
+            return int(result or 0)
+        except ImportError: pass
+    print(f"error: unrecognized command '{cmd}'",file=sys.stderr)
+    return 2
+
+if __name__=="__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Small, dependency-free implementation of Taplo's common formatting behavior."""
import re

def format_text(src, options=None):
    opts = {"compact_entries": False, "compact_arrays": True, "array_trailing_comma": True,
            "trailing_newline": True, "crlf": False, "allowed_blank_lines": 2}
    opts.update(options or {})
    # Normalize line endings, then format each statement while retaining comments and table order.
    lines = src.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").split("\n")
    out=[]
    blank=0
    for line in lines:
        s=line.strip()
        if not s:
            blank += 1
            if blank <= int(opts.get("allowed_blank_lines", 2)) and out and out[-1] != "": out.append("")
            continue
        blank=0
        if s.startswith("#") or (s.startswith("[") and s.endswith("]")):
            out.append(s); continue
        # Locate assignment = outside quoted strings and nested values.
        quote=None; esc=False; depth=0; eq=-1
        for i,c in enumerate(s):
            if quote:
                if esc: esc=False
                elif c=='\\' and quote=='"': esc=True
                elif c==quote: quote=None
            elif c in ('"', "'"): quote=c
            elif c in "[{(": depth+=1
            elif c in "]})": depth-=1
            elif c=="=" and depth==0: eq=i; break
        if eq >= 0:
            key=s[:eq].strip(); val=s[eq+1:].strip()
            # Normalize whitespace around separators inside arrays/inline tables without changing strings.
            val=_normalize(val, bool(opts.get("compact_arrays", True)), bool(opts.get("compact_inline_tables", False)), bool(opts.get("compact_entries", False)))
            s=key + ("=" if opts.get("compact_entries") else " = ") + val
            if opts.get("indent_entries") and any(x.startswith("[") for x in out):
                s=str(opts.get("indent_string", "  "))+s
        out.append(s)
    if opts.get("reorder_keys"):
        start=0
        while start < len(out):
            if not out[start] or out[start].startswith("#") or out[start].startswith("["):
                start += 1; continue
            end=start
            while end<len(out) and out[end] and not out[end].startswith("#") and not out[end].startswith("["): end+=1
            out[start:end]=sorted(out[start:end], key=lambda x:x.split("=",1)[0].strip())
            start=end
    while out and out[-1]=="": out.pop()
    result="\n".join(out)
    if opts.get("trailing_newline", True) and result: result += "\n"
    if opts.get("crlf"): result=result.replace("\n","\r\n")
    return result

def _normalize(s, compact_arrays, compact_inline_tables, compact_entries):
    # Token-wise whitespace normalization for arrays and inline tables.
    res=[]; quote=None; esc=False
    for i,c in enumerate(s):
        if quote:
            res.append(c)
            if esc: esc=False
            elif c=='\\' and quote=='"': esc=True
            elif c==quote: quote=None
            continue
        if c in ('"',"'"): quote=c; res.append(c); continue
        if c=='[':
            res.append("[" if compact_arrays else "[ ")
            continue
        if c==']':
            if compact_arrays and res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
            res.append("]"); continue
        if c=='{': res.append("{" + ("" if compact_inline_tables else " ")); continue
        if c=='}':
            if compact_inline_tables:
                if res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
            elif res and res[-1] not in " {":
                res.append(" ")
            res.append("}"); continue
        if c==',':
            while res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
            res.append(", "); continue
        if c=='=':
            while res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
            res.append("=" if compact_entries else " = "); continue
        if c=='#':
            while res and res[-1]==' ': res.pop()
            res.append(" #"); res.extend(s[i+1:]); break
        if c.isspace():
            if not res or res[-1] in "[{,= ": continue
            res.append(" "); continue
        if res and res[-1]==' ' and compact_arrays and c in "]}": res.pop()
        res.append(c)
    return ''.join(res).strip()
"}

{"chunk_id":"2f0191","wall_time_seconds":0.000004083,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":916,"output":"# Configuration File

Taplo supports configuration via file, unsurprisingly it uses the TOML format.

By default, every tool looks for one in the working directory or the root of the workspace by the following names (in precedence order):

- `.taplo.toml`
- `taplo.toml`

## Include

The `include` property is an array of [glob](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glob_(programming)>) path strings that are relative to the working directory (or root of the workspace),
the matched files are included in the operations by the tools unless explicitly overwritten. The pattern supports globstars (`**`) for recursive search.

If this property is omitted, `TOML` files will be searched in the entire child directory tree from the root.

::: warning

If `include` is present but empty, **no files will be included**.

:::

```toml
include = ["Cargo.toml", "some_directory/**/*.toml"]
```

## Exclude

The `exclude` property has the same semantics as `include` and takes precedence over it.

The following will exclude `Cargo.toml` from the includes written above, so files matching `some_directory/**/*.toml` will be included only.

```toml
exclude = ["Cargo.toml"]
```

## Formatting Options

The `formatting` table contains optional [formatting options](./formatter-options.md) for the formatter:

```toml
[formatting]
align_entries = false
```

## Schema

The `schema` table consists of only two keys:

- `path`: the path of the schema, this can be either path to a local file or an URL with the schemes `taplo`, `http` or `https`. (`file` scheme is also accepted, it is the same as specifying a local path)
- `enabled`: whether to enable the schema or not (`true` if omitted).

An example:

```toml
[schema]
path = "./path/to/schema.json"
enabled = true
```

Or a configuration that uses a built-in schema:

```toml
[schema]
path = "taplo://taplo.toml"
```

Or a remote one:

```toml
[schema]
path = "https://example.com/my_schema.json"
```

## Rules

The `rule` array of tables consist of rules that overwrite the above configuration based on some conditions.
Thus it has the same `formatting` and `schema` settings, and the `include` and `exclude` with the same semantics as their [global variants](#include), however this time they are used to determine whether the rule applies.

Additionally, `keys` of a rule is an array of dotted keys that scope the rule to a specific part within a single document.
The keys also support glob patterns.

::: tip

In case of overlapping rules, the last defined rule always takes precedence.

:::

Let's say we want to sort our `Cargo` dependencies, but nothing else, here is how we would do that:

```toml
[formatting]
reorder_keys = false

[[rule]]
include = ["**/Cargo.toml"]
keys = ["dependencies"]

[rule.formatting]
reorder_keys = true
```
# Configuration

## Log Level

Taplo uses the Rust `tracing` library for configurable logging features and respects the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. All logs regardless of log level are printed to the standard error output.

In most cases you might wish to disable logging below a certain log level.
As an example if you wish to only see error messages, you can do the following:

```sh
RUST_LOG=error taplo lint foo.toml
```

The available log levels:

- `trace`
- `debug`
- `info`
- `warn`
- `error`

## Configuration File

<!-- TODO: config link -->

Taplo CLI, by default, searches the current working directory for a Taplo configuration file. This behaviour can be disabled by either supplying `--no-auto-config` or `--config <path>` flags. The `TAPLO_CONFIG` environmental variable can also be used to set the configuration, but the `--config` flag will take precedence.
"}

content.text:
## Handoff summary

**Goal:** Recreate `/opt/reference/executable` (Taplo CLI) in Python 3.10 using only bundled docs and observed CLI behavior. No source browsing, external packages, or runtime use of the reference binary. Do not run `compile.sh`.

**Workspace:** `/workspace`. Shared branch is `team/main`; fetch before editing, then merge and push with `git push team HEAD:main`. My latest local sync was `18153b7`, with a clean worktree. Other agents may have pushed since; fetch first.

**Implemented and pushed:** CLI dispatcher, formatter, config, completions, get, lint, TOML-test decoder, and LSP modules are integrated on shared main. Formatter supports stdin and files, check/diff, config options, key/array ordering, alignment, wrapping, inline table expansion, syntax errors, and file rewrites for `--diff`. Lint includes syntax and duplicate checks plus schema validation. Local verification used `python3 -m py_compile *.py` and direct reference comparisons.

**Important decisions/findings:**

- Python 3.10 lacks `tomllib`; the implementation uses a local parser in `tomltest.py`.
- Reference version is `taplo 0.10.0`.
- `format -` reads stdin; `format` with no file arguments is silent. Empty stdin with `format -` outputs a newline.
- File `format --diff` prints a patch and rewrites the file; `--check --diff` prints a patch without rewriting.
- `lint --schema` expects a URL (e.g. `file:///...`); a plain absolute path gets “relative URL without a base.”
- `compile.sh` is evaluator-owned; do not run it.
- Keep coordinating through the `group` tools and push changes to shared main.

**Next steps:**

1. Fetch and merge the newest `team/main`; the group feed had activity after my last sync.
2. Review schema validation diagnostics and LSP syntax diagnostics, which were recently being improved.
3. Continue probing uncovered edge cases against the reference, fix differences, and push each change.
4. Re-run `python3 -m py_compile *.py` after integration and check the worktree before finishing.
